name: Mount Horeb
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Mount Horeb, WI 2026
seo_desc: Christmas events for kids in Mount Horeb, WI for 2026: Trollidays, Santa Day, the Silent Parade and Cave of Lights, with dates checked on host sites.
lede: The Troll Capital of the World dresses its Trollway for the holidays, with window scenes, a Santa Shop Hop, a silent parade of fire trucks and a lit cave nearby.
celebrates: Mount Horeb celebrates December with Trollidays, a month long program from the Mount Horeb Area Chamber of Commerce. Local artists create festive window scenes for downtown storefronts, and an interactive map and a just for fun scavenger hunt send families looking for them. A Santa Troll hides in downtown shops for the Santa Shop Hop, with collectible troll ornaments as weekly prizes. The Mount Horeb Welcome Center at 300 East Main Street sells a collectible troll ornament, and the chamber hosts Elves Night Out with free trolley rides. Mount Horeb Fire and EMS adds a silent parade of decorated fire trucks and tree lighting.
lastyear: The Mount Horeb Fire Department held the 36th annual Silent Parade and Tree Lighting on Saturday, December 6, 2025, starting at 5 pm, according to its event listing. The parade has long been a procession of decorated fire trucks without sirens, ending at Grandma Foster Park where the community tree is illuminated. Its news page records the same tradition in earlier years, including the 33rd annual lighting in 2022 and the 30th in 2018.
facts: Mount Horeb took shape in 1861, when English immigrant and Methodist minister George Wright set up the local post office and named the village after the biblical mountain. Norwegian immigrants arrived in large numbers from the 1850s on. The Chicago and Tomah Railway ran its first train through in 1881. In the 1970s and 1980s hand carved trolls began appearing outside a gift shop on Main Street, and the Trollway grew from there. Today more than 40 troll sculptures line the village streets.
trains: Railroads shaped Mount Horeb: the Chicago and Tomah Railway ran its first train through in 1881, connecting local farms and businesses to Madison, and for decades passenger and freight trains were part of daily life. Families who want a Christmas train ride today can drive northwest to the Mid-Continent Railway Museum in North Freedom, which runs Santa Express weekends in the season. Check the museum's page for dates and ticket details before you go.
train_links: Seven-mile steam and diesel train rides at North Freedom, with Santa Express weekends in the season.
traditions: Local artists decorate storefront windows with playful trolls all December.
Shoppers who spot Santa Troll in a downtown shop can enter to win collectible troll ornaments.
The chamber hosts an evening of holiday specials and free trolley rides on the Trollway.
Decorated fire trucks roll without sirens to Grandma Foster Park for the community tree lighting.
Cave of the Mounds decorates its cave for the holidays each season.
kidfact: Mount Horeb has more than 40 hand carved trolls along its streets, and in December the trolls get festive window scenes of their own.
faq: Why is Mount Horeb called the Troll Capital of the World?

Norwegian immigrants settled the area from the 1850s, and in the 1970s and 1980s hand carved trolls from Scandinavian folklore began appearing outside a Main Street gift shop. More trolls followed, the street became the Trollway, and the village adopted the title.

Trollidays is the Mount Horeb Area Chamber of Commerce's December celebration. It includes festive window scenes by local artists, a scavenger hunt, the Santa Troll Shop Hop, collectible ornaments and Elves Night Out with free trolley rides. See the listing below for 2026 details.
Where is the Mount Horeb Welcome Center?

The Welcome Center is at 300 East Main Street, on the Trollway. It is the hub for Elves Night Out, and it sells collectible Trollway ornaments and other troll themed gifts, with proceeds going to improvements at the center.

It is a parade of decorated fire trucks that moves through downtown without sirens, hosted by Mount Horeb Fire and EMS. It ends at Grandma Foster Park, where the community tree is lit. In 2026 it is the 37th annual parade.
How far is Mount Horeb from Madison?
The Mount Horeb chamber describes the village as about 30 minutes west of Madison. Cave of the Mounds, home of Cave of Lights, is just outside nearby Blue Mounds.

intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Mount Horeb for 2026, and here is what he found: 4 family events, 1 of them free. The magic runs from the Cave of Lights at Cave of the Mounds (November 26 to January 31) and Mount Horeb Trollidays (all of December) through Santa Day at the library and the Silent Parade and Community Tree Lighting (both December 5) to Elves Night Out (December 10). We check every date on the host's own website, and each listing links straight there.

What Rally found in Mount Horeb

  • 4 Christmas events for kids in Mount Horeb
  • 1 free event: the Silent Parade and Community Tree Lighting (December 5), where a card or canned food earns free hot cocoa
  • Meet Santa: Santa Day at Mount Horeb Public Library (December 5, 10 am to 1 pm) and the Santa Shop Hop during Trollidays
  • Parade and lights: the 37th annual Silent Parade ending at Grandma Foster Park and the Cave of Lights in Blue Mounds
  • Trollidays: window scenes, a scavenger hunt and Elves Night Out with free trolley rides on December 10
